extracted.intended_audience: editors, copyeditors, proofreaders, typesetters, and authors preparing scholarly/professional manuscripts
extracted.subtask_description: Apply the University of Chicago Manual of Style rules for punctuation, capitalization, typography, hyphenation, citations, tables, and other editorial/typographic conventions for preparing or evaluating printed/typed manuscripts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Capitalization (general and proper nouns)
rubrics_metrics.description: Capitalization of proper names and nouns: 'Proper names: capitalization of, 1'; 'Names: alphabetization of, 240; Christian, to be spelled out, 93; familiar, applied to particular persons, to be capitalized, 21; proper, capitalization of, 1.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance covers capitalization for geographical names, divisions, institutions, organizations, governmental departments, religious denominations and creeds, dynasties, epochs, events, movements, schools, philosophical/literary/artistic names, regiments, parties, offices, titles, honors and decorations, sacred books, tribes/peoples/races, parks/squares/thoroughfares, and other categories. See many specific entries (e.g., 'geographical names, capitalization of, 4, 5, 6').

rubrics_metrics.name: Capitalization of titles and 'principal words' in titles
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Titles of publications: capitalization of principal words in, 41'; 'Principal words: capitalization of, in titles of publications, 41; definition of, 41.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies which words in titles are capitalized, treatment of subtitles and subdivisions, when titles are italicized versus roman-quoted, treatment across languages (English, Latin, French, Italian, Spanish, German, Scandinavian, Danish, Dutch), handling of newspapers (definite article not part of title), and special rules for shorter works (poems, essays, papers, lectures, pamphlets, plays, tracts, treatises, proceedings, serial titles). Also addresses treatment of initial words, first words after a colon, and last words in titles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Italics: when to use
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Italics: defined, 254; rules for use of, 58-73.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lists many applications: emphasis; words/phrases from foreign languages; titles of books and other works; titles of newspapers; names of genera and species; names of catalogues, constellations, and stars; letters designating unknown quantities; letters referring to letters in illustrations; initial word 'Resolved' in resolutions; words 'See' and 'See also' in indexing; certain symbols (shillings and pence); 'for' and 'read' in errata; and to indicate continuation of article/chapter. Notes that italics need not be used in lengthy bibliographical lists and gives cross-references for many specific cases (e.g., legal causes, ships, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Dashes: definition and usage
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Dashes: definition and illustrations of use of, 166; different sizes of, explained, 261; rules for use of, 166-75.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains emphatic dash uses: to denote break/stop/transition/change in sentence; to precede summarizing clauses; to indicate implication of word/phrase; to indicate pause, epigrammatic turn, or transition; to connect numbers; for emphasis; and special use at end of word/phrase when implied at beginning of succeeding paragraphs. Also distinguishes em-dash and en-dash forms and cross-references spacing/typographic sizes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hyphens and hyphenation rules
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Hyphens: number of consecutive, allowable at ends of lines, 217; rules for use of, 182-214.' 'Hyphenization, rules for, 182-214.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers when to hyphenate compounds and prefixes (pre-, post-, re-, co-, self-, semi-, tri-, super-, sub-, etc.), use of hyphen to indicate syllable division, avoidance of dividing hyphenated words, list of hyphenated words, when prefix/suffix not complete is indicated by hyphen, and special compound categories ('mother,' 'father,' 'house,' 'store,' 'work,' etc.). Also addresses hyphen leaders and number of hyphens at line ends.

rubrics_metrics.name: Division of words and dividing (syllabification)
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Division of words: rules for, 215-31; systems of division, 221; use of hyphen to indicate, 182; avoidance of unnecessary, 215; on two letters, to be avoided, 216; of foreign words, 231.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rules include avoiding division at end of penultimate line or bottom of recto page, not dividing on certain consonants (J, G soft, soft c or g), treating diphthongs as one letter, vowel division guidance (put single vowel forming separate syllable in first line), special guidance for Greek/Latin/foreign words, etymological/derivational division to be avoided, and typographic placement of divisional marks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quotation marks and quotations (including punctuation placement)
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Quotation marks. not to be used in connection with reduced citations, 87; exception to this rule, 75; placing of colon in connection with, 136, of comma, 162; of ellipsis, 181, of exclamation point, 128, of interrogation point, 130, of period, 126; rules for use of, 74-01; to be omitted in references to Preface, Index, etc., 82; use of double and single, 91.' 'Quotations, how to treat, 74-01; first word of, lower-cased when connected with previous sentence, 57.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies when to use or omit quotation marks (including single vs double), rules for punctuation that accompanies quoted material (periods, commas, colons, semicolons, question/exclamation marks, ellipses), treatment of reduced citations, and capitalization of the first word in quoted material when integrated into preceding sentence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ellipses: use and treatment
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Ellipses. rules for use of, r80-81; to be treated as part of quotation, 88, 181, use of, to indicate omissions, 180.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describes how ellipses indicate omissions within quotations, how they should be treated typographically as part of the quotation (including spacing and punctuation interplay), and cross-references to quotation punctuation rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parentheses, brackets, and interpolations
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Parentheses: rules for use of, 176-77; use of, for parenthetical clauses, 177 (cf. 150, 167); within parentheses, use of brackets for, 178.' 'Interpolations, use of brackets for, 178.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gives rules for parenthetical clauses, nesting brackets inside parentheses, placing of punctuation relative to parentheses, and use of brackets to indicate interpolations or editorial explanations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comma usage in clauses and enumerations
rubrics_metrics.description: 'First words after a colon, when capitalized...'; 'Use of comma in connection with if-clauses, 144; parenthetical clauses, 150; participial clauses, 148; phrases adjectival, 152; conjunctional, etc., 145; sequences of three or more links, use of comma before “and,” “or,” and “nor” in, 143.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides syntactic rules for when commas are required or omitted: after signatures and dates, before 'of' in certain constructions, in enumerations and sequences, to separate clauses (if/participial/parenthetical), and special rules for introductory elements and clauses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Semicolon usage
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Semicolon: separating two or more distinct clauses in enumerations, 36, illustration of use of, compared with that of comma, 137, placing of, in connection with quotation marks, 140; rules for use of, 137-40; use of, in enumerations, 138, to mark division of sentence, 137.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains semicolon's role in separating complex list items and independent clauses, its placement relative to quotation marks, and examples contrasting semicolon use vs comma use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Periods and terminal punctuation
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Period. placing of, in connection with quotation marks, 126, rules for use of, 122-26; to be omitted after headlines, 125, after Roman numerals, 124; of abbreviations, 123.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies when periods are required or omitted (abbreviations, headlines, numerals), and how terminal punctuation interacts with quotation marks and parenthetical indices; cross-references to other punctuation rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interrogation point / question mark usage
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Doubt, use of interrogation point to express, 129'; 'Interrogation point, use of, 129-30'; 'Questions direct, to be followed by interrogation point, 129; indirect, not to be followed by interrogation point, 129.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rules for using question marks for direct questions and rhetorical/doubtful expressions, and their placement with quotation marks and parentheses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclamation point usage
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Exclamation point, rules for use of, 127-28.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies use for outcry, emphasis, irony, and placement with quotation marks; cross-reference to ironic usage and exclamatory 'Oh'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apostrophes and possessives / contractions
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Contraction of word, use of apostrophe in, 163.' 'Possessive case, how formed, 113, 164.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers use of apostrophe for contractions and omissions, rules for forming possessives (including proper names ending in sibilants), omission indicated by apostrophe, and avoidance of confusing omissions in dates/numbers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Numbers, numerals, ordinals, and statistics
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Numbers: commencing a sentence, to be spelled out, 96; consecutive, treatment of, 159, 173; in connected groups to be treated alike, 94; in groups six or more to be set in figures, 94; of less than three digits to be spelled out in ordinary reading-matter, 94; round, treatment of, 95; use of comma after thousands, 159; use of comma to separate, 154; use of dash for 'to' connecting, 173.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes rules for Arabic vs Roman numerals (spacing at beginning of lines/headlines), ordinals, omission of period after Roman numerals, formation of plurals of numerals, treatment of percentages (per cent to be expressed in figures), and handling of numbers in statistical columns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dates and time notation
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Dates; hundreds repeated, when and when not, 173; of publications, to follow volume numbers...; st, d, and nd to be omitted from, 102; use of comma between month and year in, 160.' 'Time: indications, how to punctuate, 1343; of day, how to treat, 98.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rules on spelling out decades and centuries, omitting ordinal indicators (st/nd/d), punctuation in datelines (comma between month and year), use of en-dash for ranges, and time-of-day formatting (a.m./p.m. spacing and small caps guidance).

rubrics_metrics.name: Abbreviations, initials, and symbols
rubrics_metrics.description: 'F., ff. (= 'following'). spacing of, 260, use of, 120.' 'Initials: of titles of publications, use of, 123, separation of, in different lines, to be avoided, 219.' 'Symbols: chemical, treatment of, 71, 123; metric, spacing of, 269; monetary, spacing of, 270; as reference indices, 232.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers when to use periods with abbreviations (omission after certain abbreviations and in classical references), spacing conventions for abbreviations and initials, punctuation/typography of metric and monetary symbols, and formatting of common bibliographic abbreviations (op. cit., ibid., loc. cit., et al.).

rubrics_metrics.name: References, citations, and bibliographies
rubrics_metrics.description: 'References, legal, list of words and phrases in, 61, literary list of words to be abbreviated in, 110 (cf. 37, 54, 237); punctuation of, etc, 237, 239, note, use of dash in connection with, 174.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gives rules for formatting literary and legal references, use of abbreviations in bibliographies, punctuation in references (including placing periods and commas), volume/page notation, use of italics in titles, treatment of 'p.' and 'vol.' abbreviations, and indexing of classical references.

rubrics_metrics.name: Footnotes, indices, and reference marks
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Footnotes: exceptions to general style for, 237, 239, note; general style for, 237; indices for references to, 232; numbering of, 239; placing of index figure, 236; rules for, 232-39; samples of, 237; to tables, 234.' 'Indices for footnote references: how to number, 240, placing of, 236; sequence of, 232, what to use for, 232.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance on footnote numbering sequences, placement of reference marks (superior figures, daggers, double daggers, paragraph/section/parallel marks), ordering of multiple indices, formatting notes attached to tables, and exceptions to general footnote style.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tables and tabular work
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Tables: columns representing totals, percentages, etc., frequently set off by different type, 241; headlines of, how to set, 249; of two columns, to be set as open, 248; of more than two, as ruled, 248; open headlines for columns in, 242; ruled, how to set, 241; rules for setting of, 241-50; rules for use of rules in, 243, 247; specimen, 250.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies open vs ruled tables, box-heads, headlines and subhead formatting, column alignment and special typesetting for totals/percentages, double rules usage, hyphen/leaders/period leaders in tables, spacing and reading-matter conventions, and specimen examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Spacing (spaces, leaders, and even spacing)
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Spaces: different sizes of, explained, 250, 261; specimen of lines spaced with different sizes of, 261.' 'Spacing: in foundry type (and general) composition, 261-64; in linotype composition, 260; in monotype composition, 259; rules for, 258-73; standard, 262; what is considered good, 262.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines space sizes (hair, thin, thick, em, en, quad, three-em/four-em, etc.), when to avoid thin- or wide-spacing, rules for spacing around symbols/figures/headlines/periods, and use of leaders (hyphen, period) in tables.

rubrics_metrics.name: Typography, type sizes, and typographical units
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Type: different parts of body of, explained, 256; names for different sizes of, 252; styles of, 253-57.' 'Point system, explanation of, 251-52; unit, typographical, explained, 251.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers typographic terminology (face, font, pica, nonpareil, em/en quads), explanation of the point system, typographic measures and units, body and shoulder/shank terminology, and guidance on style families and sizes (examples and specimen lists).

rubrics_metrics.name: Proofs, proof-correction, and making up (make-up)
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Proofs, description of, 285-89.' 'Proofreaders: hints to, pp. 117-19; marks of, p 123.' 'Make-up, defined, 290.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines galley/page/plate/plate-proof/foundry-proof/foul proof, describes proofreading marks and common corrections, offers hints for copyholders and proofreaders, and explains make-up/revise/revise stages in production.

rubrics_metrics.name: Headings, headlines, side-heads, and running heads
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Headings, described, 279-83.' 'Headlines; of tables, how to set, 249; omission of period after, 125; spacing of, 271; word "continued" following, to be set in italics, 73.' 'Side-heads: defined, 280; omission of period after, 125; use of in connection with, 172; use of lower case in, 56.' 'Running-heads defined, 283; omission of period after, 125, hint for setting of, 283.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance on formatting section/side/head/running heads, omission of terminal periods, capitalization/roman-quote/italic conventions for headings, spacing and indentation conventions (pyramid, flush, plain paragraph), and use of small caps in headings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Poetry and verse formatting
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Poems: capitalization of first word of each line in English, 34; of first word of each paragraph in Greek and Latin, 34; capitalization of principal words in titles of, 41; titles of shorter, to be roman-quoted, 81; poetry. indention of, 275; quotations from, when to reduce, 85; when to run into the text, 85.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers line-level capitalization, stanza and paragraph indentation, formatting of short vs long poems (roman-quoted vs italicized), when to reduce quotations from verse, rhymed-line indentation and handling of cycles of poems and their titles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indexes and indexing rules
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Indexing. italicizing of "See," "See also," in cross-references, 62; rules for, 240; treatment of prefixes and particles in proper nouns, 240.' 'Index figure, placing of, 236.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides rules for alphabetical treatment of names (treatment of 'Mac', 'Mc', 'Van', 'Von', 'O’', 'St.'), placement and form of index figures, use of small caps, and italicization in cross-references; guidance for handling foreign particles and umlauts in indexing and indexing of initials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Names, particles, and treatment of compound names
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Mac,' 'Mc,' 'M’,' rule for treatment of, 240; 'Van,' rule for treatment of, 3, 240; 'Von,' rule for treatment of, 3, 240; 'O’,' rule for treatment of, in indexing, 240.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rules for capitalization and indexing of surnames with particles and prefixes (Mac/Mc/M’, Van, Von, O’, St.), guidelines for when to capitalize particles, and how to alphabetize and form possessives for such names.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific, biological, and paleontological names and terms
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Scientific terms, use of capitals in, 46; of italics, 71.' 'Species, scientific names of: use of capitals in, 46; of italics, 71.' 'Paleontological terms: use of capitals in, 46; of italics, 72.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies italicization for genus/species names, capitalization rules for scientific and paleontological terms, and exceptions when English derivatives from scientific names are lowercased.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foreign languages and translations
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Foreign languages: division of words in, 231; English translation accompanying word, phrase, or passage cited from, to be noted, 78; sentences and passages quoted from, how to treat, 59,85; words from foreign languages, use of italics for, 59; words and phrases borrowed from, incorporated into English, how to treat, 59.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance covers italicization of foreign words, provision of English equivalents, treatment of foreign-language titles and their capitalization, use/non-use of ligatures in Latin/German/French, and division/ hyphenation rules for foreign words.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal and juridical references and titles
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Juridical acts, laws, bills, capitalization of names of, 18.' 'Titles of legal causes and proceedings, italicized, 63.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers capitalization and formatting of laws, bills, treaties, juridical acts, and legal case titles (italicization), plus punctuation and abbreviation conventions in legal references.

rubrics_metrics.name: Units, measures, and monetary notation
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Units of measurement, abbreviations for, 111; spelled with lower-case initial letter, 55.' 'Metric: symbols, how to treat, 123; spacing of, 269; system, designation of weights and measures in, 112.' 'Monetary symbols, spacing of, 270; Money, sums of, how to treat, 97.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rules for abbreviation and spacing of units (metric and imperial), presentation of sums of money, percent/per cent usage (figures vs words), and typographic spacing conventions around symbols.

rubrics_metrics.name: Titles of offices, ranks, and honorifics
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Titles: academic, to be abbreviated, 22, civil and military, capitalization of, 21; honorary, 21; in direct address, 21; of nobility, 21; not capitalized when spelled out, 22; preceding names, to be spelled out, 92; list of exceptions, 92.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies capitalization for titles when used as part of a name vs generic references, when to abbreviate academic and civil titles, treatment of 'vice', 'ex-', 'elect', 'general', 'lieutenant' as parts of titles, and special University of Chicago usages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tables of contents, parts/divisions, and roman-quoting of subdivisions
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Divisions of publications, titles of: capitalization of principal words in, 41, to be roman-quoted, 82.' 'Parts (of books, etc.), titles of: capitalization of principal words in, 41; to be roman-quoted, 82.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guides formatting of subdivisions, parts, series, serial titles, and when to use roman quotes versus italics for subdivisions and internal divisions of works.

rubrics_metrics.name: Typographic marks used as indices (dagger, double dagger, paragraph mark, section mark, parallel mark)
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Dagger, use of, for footnote index, 232.' 'Double dagger, use of, for footnote index, 232.' 'Paragraph mark: spacing of, 269, use of, for footnote index, 232.' 'Section mark spacing of, 269; use of, for footnote index, 232.' 'Parallel mark, use of, for footnote index, 232.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies which symbols may be used as reference indices for notes, order/sequence of such symbols, spacing and typographic treatment, and guidance on superior figures vs symbol indices.
